title: Mathematical Methods in Particle Size Distributions for Catalysts Applications
content: Metal nanoparticles are essential in heterogenous catalysis, with their size directly influencing catalytic performance, including activity, selectivity, and stability [1]. Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) is a widely employed technique to analyse particle size distributions, providing images to measure individual particle dimensions [2]. However, this process is often time-consuming and requires substantial experimental resources. Research has demonstrated the application of mathematical methods to retrieve particle size, using digital micro-mirror device-based detectors, highlighting the potential of mathematical methods in particle size analysis [3]. Traditionally, particle size distributions are represented as histograms, which depend on binning parameters and the number of measurements. While histograms rely on hundreds to thousands of measurements for statistical accuracy, this requirement poses a challenge and underscore the need for methods that can reduce the required number of measurements while maintaining accuracy.
